s1022: Which of these combinations of road signs is placed outside a built-up area, 150-300 metres before a railway crossing without a barrier, on the left side of the road?
s1023: According to paragraphs 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4.1–1.4.6 of Annex 1 to the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic: road sign 1.1 "Level crossing with barrier" warns of an approaching railway crossing with a barrier. 1.2 "Level crossing without barrier" warns of an approaching railway crossing without a barrier. 1.4.1–1.4.6 "Approaching a railway crossing" gives the driver an additional warning, outside built-up areas, of an approaching railway crossing. According to subparagraphs "a" and "f" of the Note to Chapter 1 of the same Annex: a) signs 1.1, 1.2 and 1.5–1.34 are placed outside built-up areas 150−300 metres before the start of the hazardous section, and in built-up areas 50–100 metres before it. If necessary, the signs are placed at another distance, which is shown on plate 8.1.1; f) signs 1.4.1−1.4.3 are placed on the right side of the road, and signs 1.4.4−1.4.6 on the left side. Signs 1.4.1 and 1.4.4 are placed, in the direction of travel, together with the main and the repeated sign 1.1 or 1.2; signs 1.4.3 and 1.4.6 together with the repeated sign 1.1 or 1.2; and signs 1.4.2 and 1.4.5 on their own, at an equal distance between the main and the repeated sign 1.1 or 1.2.
